title: Formal statements read a sign in its bounded context and cite the workflow's residue
situation: The corpus's formal statements of its principle (VISION's σ*, MODEL's invariants, the prime principle and the signify, probe, exemplify and introspect skills) take what a sign fires from the sign alone and define the residue one-sidedly, while the corpus concepts now read every sign within its bounded context and measure it by the workflow's residue.
decision: Every formal statement names the bounded context a sign is read in as κ, κ(c) for a concept's: what a sign fires is fired(n, κ), never fired(n); a cold read gives the reader the sign with κ's name and subject and nothing of the intended concept. The residue is cited, never restated: residue(c) is the workflow's residue of c, its name read in κ(c), referenced with the cells' existing `@` reference form (`residue @ workflow`) or in prose as the workflow's residue. σ* is the sign with the smallest residue in its context, any length tie-break and mint fallback kept. α is injective within each context, not across contexts. Code comments that state the residue one-sidedly are reworded to cite it; the cold-oracle script and the static witnesses keep their behaviour.
consequences: Restating the principle changes no sign and runs no oracle; the cold-oracle script still sends a fragment without its context's name and subject, a follow-up for realizing the oracle, and the static PARSIMONIOUS witness still checks one half of the residue.
